name: Brute Force
description: Repeated authentication failures may be consistent with password guessing or brute-force activity.
response: Review source IP and target account
Apply account protection policy after analyst validation
confidence_note: A 4625 event alone does not prove brute force.

name: Valid Accounts
tactic: Initial Access, Persistence, Privilege Escalation, Defense Evasion
description: Successful logons using valid accounts may be relevant when paired with unusual source, time or privilege activity.
response: Verify account owner and logon source
Review sign-in history and privilege use
confidence_note: A successful logon is not inherently malicious.

name: Account Manipulation
description: Unexpected account creation or group membership changes may indicate account manipulation.
response: Revoke unauthorised changes only after approval
confidence_note: Legitimate administration can produce these events.

name: Clear Windows Event Logs
description: Security log clearing can remove evidence and warrants prompt investigation.
response: Check centralised logs and other telemetry

name: Windows Service
description: Unexpected service installation may indicate persistence or execution through a Windows service.
response: Inspect service name, binary path and signer
Quarantine only through approved response procedure
confidence_note: Software installation is not automatically malicious.

name: PowerShell
description: PowerShell process or command evidence can be relevant to script-based execution, especially with suspicious command-line indicators.
response: Capture command line and parent process
Check script block logs where enabled
